briefFidelity: FAIL, and the failure is one recurring element. Blind, before reading anything, I wrote that the collection's 'one real gesture' is a diagonal staircase of small squares stepping away from the host shape 'like a comet tail or a sprocket run', on 9548, 9727, 10264, 10980 and downward on 9190. The brief forbids that element three separate times: 'one form, centred, and almost nothing else' (it is a second form), 'nothing decorative, nothing incidental' (it is purely incidental -- it carries no structure and supports no mass), and 'the single form held well clear of every edge' (it is not merely near the edge, it is CUT by it on 9548's top, 10980's left, 10264's right and 9190's bottom). Five of twelve tokens, 42 percent of the set, break all three at once, and they are precisely the five that are most distinctive at browse size. The remaining seven -- 9011, 9369, 9906, 10085, 10443, 10622 and marginally 10801 -- do read as STELE: one centred mass, deep empty margin, austere. The commissioned object exists in this collection; it is not what the collection is. A stele with a sprocket tail running off the edge of the stone is not a stele.
composition: Split into two incompatible halves. On the quiet seeds the brief's compositional idea is genuinely achieved: 10085, 10443, 10622 and 9906 sit as a single mass in the centre with a wide dark margin, and the emptiness reads as intended rather than as an unfilled frame. On the tailed seeds there is no focal hierarchy at all, and worse, the hierarchy is inverted -- the cascade on 10264 and 9190 is the lightest value anywhere in the collection, so the eye lands on the appendage and not on the mass it is appended to. The frame is used in neither half: seven tokens ignore their edges entirely and five collide with them by accident. 10801 is a third case, an octagon with several rotated squares tumbled inside it, which is busy internally in a way the brief's 'almost nothing else' does not admit.
collectionCoherence: This axis holds. Every token shares one vocabulary (flat hard-edged primitives, alpha-blended, no line work, no texture), one ground (flat charcoal), and one narrow value band, and I identified all three blind as the constants across the twelve. Nobody would mistake 10622 and 9548 for different projects. The reservation is that the set reads as two sub-families rather than one -- quiet centred steles (9011, 9369, 9906, 10085, 10443, 10622) and tailed compositions (9548, 9727, 10264, 10980, 9190) -- which look like two different briefs answered with the same rendering kit rather than twelve answers to one brief.
palette: Right in hue, wrong in count. The warm-neutral band -- taupe, putty, oatmeal, bone -- on flat charcoal is austere and looks chosen, and the ground supports the drawing rather than competing with it, which is what was asked. But the brief says 'two values and a ground, no more', and the medium here manufactures values as a by-product: every translucent overlap creates a new step, so 9011 neutral carries five or six distinct greys between square, hexagon, their intersection and the two nested inner shapes, and 10801 carries more. 9190 and 10264 then add a near-white that is the brightest value in the entire collection, sitting on top of the mid-greys. 10085 and 10443 are close to the two-values-plus-ground the brief specified; most of the set is not, and the excess is structural to the technique rather than incidental.
seedVariation: Fails in both directions the axis names. Too narrow among the quiet seeds: 10085 (hexagon), 10443 (diamond with a circle) and 10622 (square with concentric squares) are so bare that they approach interchangeability once the inner shapes drop out, and 9011 and 9906 are the same nested-polygon gesture at a different rotation. Too wide between the families: 10264 and 9190, with bright clustered cascades crowding a corner, are not variations of 10085, they are a different kind of picture. The brief asked that 'tokens differ chiefly in the silhouette of the single form', and silhouette does vary correctly -- square 9011, diamond 9906, hexagon 10085, circle 9369, octagon 10801 -- but that is not what actually distinguishes the twelve in the eye. What distinguishes them is having a tail or not having one, which is the axis the brief closed.
thumbnailSurvival: The state rows survive 120px very well and the seed row does not. On holdout-states-120 all four seeds read as three unmistakably different images and the direction of change is legible without the labels. On holdout-seeds-120 the twelve collapse to four or five perceptual classes: plain grey polygon (9011, 9906, 10085, 10443, 10622, and 10801 whose interior tumble mushes to a flat mottle), polygon-with-tail (9548, 9727, 10980), bright corner cluster (10264, 9190) and disc (9369). Every nested interior shape is gone at browse size -- 10622 is a plain grey square and nothing more. Under most briefs that is a fatal thinness; under THIS brief a bare centred polygon is the commissioned object, so I do not count the quietness against it. What I do count is that the only thing carrying seed identity at the size the work is actually seen is the forbidden element.
marketResponse: Delivered, visibly, and then over-delivered past what was asked. Blind I described stress as contraction and dimming and recovery as expansion and brightening, which is the brief's breathing exactly: 9369's disc shrinks to roughly a third of its neutral area under stress and swells to nearly fill the cell in recovery; 9011 contracts and expands; it reads at 120px on all four seeds. But the brief says the market should change 'the form's scale rather than its complexity', and complexity is exactly what changes on the tailed seeds. 9548's tail is four blocks at neutral, amputated to a single stub under stress, and back to four and brighter in recovery. 9190's cascade goes from a short run to two blocks to a long bright slab. That is a changing element COUNT, not a changing size, and it is the one behaviour the brief singled out to exclude. Value also moves with state, which 'two values and a ground' does not leave room for.
tokenIdentity: Holds on three of the four state seeds and breaks on the fourth in the most costly possible place. 9369 is a disc in all three states, 9548 a diamond, 9190 a square-based mass -- same object, different size. But 9011's outer silhouette goes square (neutral) to hexagon (stress) to square (recovery): under stress the outer square drops away almost entirely and the hexagon that was behind it becomes the read shape, which at 120px is simply a different polygon. The brief reserves silhouette for seed identity -- 'tokens differ chiefly in the silhouette of the single form' -- so market state here is spending the one axis that was supposed to tell tokens apart. That is the 'composition rearranging itself' the brief named, occurring in the exact place the brief warned about it.
artifacts: The drawing itself is clean -- no mush, no vanished strokes, no aliasing, no overlap that reads as a bug, and the alpha stacking is consistent everywhere. All the damage is at the frame and all of it belongs to the staircase: 9548's topmost block is sliced by the upper edge in both neutral and recovery; 10980's tail is cut off at the left edge; 10264's bright cluster is cut at the right edge; 9190's cascade runs off the bottom in neutral and considerably further off it in recovery. I flagged these blind as reading like overflow rather than deliberate bleed, and the reason is that the rest of every frame is untouched dark margin -- a work that ignores its edges everywhere else cannot claim a bleed at the one place it collides. No clipping occurs on any of the seven tailless tokens.
reasoning: The brief asked for a stele: one form, centred, austere, held well clear of every edge, two values and a ground, breathing by scale alone. Seven of the twelve tokens are that, and the scale response is real and reads at browse size -- this is not incompetent work and I am not refusing it for being quiet, because quiet is what was ordered. I am refusing it because the element that gives the collection its personality is the element the brief prohibited, and it breaks three explicit instructions simultaneously. The diagonal staircase on 9548, 9727, 10264, 10980 and 9190 is a second form where the brief said one, it is pure incidental decoration where the brief said none, and it is cut by the frame edge where the brief said the form must be held well clear of every edge. It then compounds this by making element count -- complexity -- the visible market response on those seeds, when the brief specifically asked for scale rather than complexity. I wrote all of this down before I read the brief, which is what makes it decisive: the tail was the first thing I named as the collection's defining gesture, and the clipping was the first thing I named as its defect. A brief this prescriptive is answered or it is not, and on 42 percent of the set it is not.
wouldChange: Four concrete changes, in order of necessity. (1) Delete the staircase entirely. It is the sole cause of the gate failure, the sole cause of every clipping artefact, and the sole reason the state response changes complexity; removing it makes 9548, 9727, 10264, 10980 and 9190 into the same austere object the other seven already are. If a tail must stay, it has to become part of the single form's silhouette -- fused, contiguous, one mass -- not an appendage stepping away from it. (2) Enforce a hard margin: compute the union bounding box of everything drawn and scale it to sit inside, say, 80 percent of the viewBox in every state, so nothing can ever touch an edge and the recovery state cannot push past what neutral fitted. (3) Cap the value ladder. Either reduce to two opaque fills plus the ground, or clamp the alpha stack so no pixel can accumulate past a second step -- the brief's 'two values and a ground, no more' is currently broken by the technique itself, not by a choice. (4) Make the state transform a pure uniform scale of a fixed element set: same shapes, same count, same fills, one multiplier. Stress must not amputate anything, recovery must not brighten anything, and 9011 must not change its outer silhouette from square to hexagon. Then push seed variation into the silhouette where the brief put it -- more distinct host polygons, and real differences in mass proportion -- because with the tail gone the twelve will otherwise read as five.
